newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee slightly up vs forward, spot dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee slightly up vs forward, spot dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee was trading slightly up against the forward dollar in late morning trade Wednesday while it was stuck in a narrow groove in the spot market, dealers said.

"Forward premiums opened down from yesterday's close and edged up slightly on some buying of forward dollar," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "But there is not much buying, I think some banks were rolling over their foreign currency deposits."
November delivery dollars were quoted at a premium of 84/87 paise in latest deals against Tuesday's close of 85/87. They opened Wednesday at 83/85 paise.
In the spot market the rupee was traded in a narrow range between 35.8275 and 35.8350 for most of the morning, dealers said.

"Most of today's trade has been between 35.830 and 35.835, with some stray deals at 35.8275," said a dealer. "The market is quiet, there is little demand for dollars and the Reserve Bank of India is yet to make an appearance today."
In latest deals, the dollar was quoted 35.830/835 rupees, after opening at 35.83/84, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
